problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=0\,.
$$
worked_solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y\operatorname{cot}⁡x & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{{2(\operatorname{cot}⁡x)}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ and $Q(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.$
